newsitem.title: Taiwan: Taiwan, General Electric in helicopter engine pact.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan, General Electric in helicopter engine pact.

text.p: signed a deal with a unit of U.S. giant General Electric Co to produce components for CT7 helicopter engines as part of an international consortium, the local contractor said.

General Electric Aircraft Engines Corp contracted Taiwan's state-owned Aerospace Industrial Development Corp to make the engine parts for S-92 helicopters made by Sikorsky Aircraft Corp, a unit of United Technologies Corp.
"We expect the deal to gain for us at least US$400 million in the next two decades," Aerospace Industrial spokesman Wu Chien-hsien told Reuters.
Wu said the state firm would hold a 7.2 percent stake in the project, jointly invested by his corporation, General Electric Aircraft Engines and the Italian carmakers Alfa Romeo and Fiat.
Wu declined to give a detailed investment breakdown.
The Taiwan contractor will produce 11 components of the engine, including turbine disks, nozzle inner ducts, cooling plates and shrouds, Wu said.

The corporation, formerly run by the military, became an ordinary state firm in July 1996. It has led development of Taiwan's Indigenous Defence Fighter and is producing 130 of the homegrown planes for the air force.
